mustard_keeper.text: Welcome to the Mustard Shop, in the Royal Arcade! In 1814 Jeremiah Colman started milling mustard by the river south of Norwich. Within a lifetime the yellow tins were in kitchens all over the world.

English mustard's made from brown and white seed, grown on Norfolk fields. The heat isn't in the seed: it happens when the ground flour meets cold water. Add hot water and you'll ruin it. Write that down.
The old saying goes that the family made their fortune from the mustard folk leave on the side of their plates. Go on, have a jar. Leave some on your plate.
Fare you well! Breathe through your mouth for the first one.

mustard_taster.text: I put a teaspoon of it on a sausage. A whole teaspoon. I can see through time now.
